newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PT Indosat to sell stake in PT Satelindo.
newsitem.headline: PT Indosat to sell stake in PT Satelindo.

text.p: State-controlled PT Indonesian Satellite Corp (Indosat) president-director Tjahjono Soerjodibroto said on Thursday the company will sell a 6.5 percent stake in PT Satelit Palapa Indonesia (Satelindo) out of its total holding of 7.5 percent.
"We plan to sell up to 6.5 percent, so we will maintain a minimum of one percent," he told reporters after the company's annual shareholders' meeting in Jakarta.

"We haven't materialised the real benefit...our share is only 7.5 percent. Secondly, due to the environment of the business itself there is some conflict of interest between us and Satelindo...where in the field we are competiting against each other," he said. "It's better for us to back out."
Soerjodibroto said the money to be raised from the sale would be used to fund Indosat's business expansion, costing some 500 billion rupiah.
He said Indosat paid 10 billion rupiah for its stake in Satelindo.
He gave no details on any prospective buyers or a price.

Soerjodibroto said U.S.-based telephone callback group USA Global Link, in which Indosat has a 20-percent stake, was planning to develop business opportunities in Europe and had invited Indosat to participate in its ventures.

"Global Link has some subsidiaries in Europe and has invited us to join. We are planning to take a 25-percent stake in one of the subsidiaries," he said, adding that the stake would cost some $15 million.
He declined to give details because of a non-disclosure agreement with the U.S. company.
He said Indosat was also looking at the possibility of venturing into two projects in Asia, adding that the company's financial advisers were to study the details.
